ESV.1: And Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me here seven altars, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
ESV.2: Balak did as Balaam had said. And Balak and Balaam offered on each altar a bull and a ram.
ESV.3: And Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your burnt offering, and I will go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever he shows me I will tell you.” And he went to a bare height,
ESV.4: and God met Balaam. And Balaam said to him, “I have arranged the seven altars and I have offered on each altar a bull and a ram.”
ESV.5: And the LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, “Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.”
ESV.6: And he returned to him, and behold, he and all the princes of Moab were standing beside his burnt offering.
ESV.7: And Balaam took up his discourse and said, “From Aram Balak has brought me, the king of Moab from the eastern mountains: ‘Come, curse Jacob for me, and come, denounce Israel!’
ESV.8: How can I curse whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce whom the LORD has not denounced?
ESV.9: For from the top of the crags I see him, from the hills I behold him; behold, a people dwelling alone, and not counting itself among the nations!
ESV.10: Who can count the dust of Jacob or number the fourth part  of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his!”
ESV.11: And Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have done nothing but bless them.”
ESV.12: And he answered and said, “Must I not take care to speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?”
ESV.13: And Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, from which you may see them. You shall see only a fraction of them and shall not see them all. Then curse them for me from there.”
ESV.14: And he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
ESV.15: Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here beside your burnt offering, while I meet the LORD over there.”
ESV.16: And the LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, “Return to Balak, and thus shall you speak.”
ESV.17: And he came to him, and behold, he was standing beside his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, “What has the LORD spoken?”
ESV.18: And Balaam took up his discourse and said, “Rise, Balak, and hear; give ear to me, O son of Zippor:
ESV.19: God is not man, that he should lie, or a son of man, that he should change his mind. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
ESV.20: Behold, I received a command to bless: he has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.
ESV.21: He has not beheld misfortune in Jacob, nor has he seen trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them.
ESV.22: God brings them out of Egypt and is for them like the horns of the wild ox.
ESV.23: For there is no enchantment against Jacob, no divination against Israel; now it shall be said of Jacob and Israel, ‘What has God wrought!’
ESV.24: Behold, a people! As a lioness it rises up and as a lion it lifts itself; it does not lie down until it has devoured the prey and drunk the blood of the slain.”
ESV.25: And Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all.”
ESV.26: But Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell you, ‘All that the LORD says, that I must do’?”
ESV.27: And Balak said to Balaam, “Come now, I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.”
ESV.28: So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the desert.
ESV.29: And Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me here seven altars and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
ESV.30: And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

NASB.1: Then Balaam said to Balak, 'Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.'
NASB.2: Balak did just as Balaam had spoken, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.
NASB.3: Then Balaam said to Balak, 'Stand beside your burnt offering, and I will go; perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever He shows me I will tell you.' So he went to a bare hill.
NASB.4: Now God met Balaam, and he said to Him, 'I have set up the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.'
NASB.5: Then the LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, 'Return to Balak, and you shall speak thus.'
NASB.6: So he returned to him, and behold, he was standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the leaders of Moab.
NASB.7: He took up his discourse and said, 'From Aram Balak has brought me, Moab's king from the mountains of the East, 'Come curse Jacob for me, And come, denounce Israel!'
NASB.8: 'How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? And how can I denounce whom the LORD has not denounced?
NASB.9: 'As I see him from the top of the rocks, And I look at him from the hills; Behold, a people [who] dwells apart, And will not be reckoned among the nations.
NASB.10: 'Who can count the dust of Jacob, Or number the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, And let my end be like his!'
NASB.11: Then Balak said to Balaam, 'What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have actually blessed them!'
NASB.12: He replied, 'Must I not be careful to speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?'
NASB.13: Then Balak said to him, 'Please come with me to another place from where you may see them, although you will only see the extreme end of them and will not see all of them; and curse them for me from there.'
NASB.14: So he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on [each] altar.
NASB.15: And he said to Balak, 'Stand here beside your burnt offering while I myself meet [the LORD] over there.'
NASB.16: Then the LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, 'Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.'
NASB.17: He came to him, and behold, he was standing beside his burnt offering, and the leaders of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, 'What has the LORD spoken?'
NASB.18: Then he took up his discourse and said, 'Arise, O Balak, and hear; Give ear to me, O son of Zippor!
NASB.19: 'God is not a man, that He should lie, Nor a son of man, that He should repent; Has He said, and will He not do it? Or has He spoken, and will He not make it good?
NASB.20: 'Behold, I have received [a command] to bless; When He has blessed, then I cannot revoke it.
NASB.21: 'He has not observed misfortune in Jacob; Nor has He seen trouble in Israel; The LORD his God is with him, And the shout of a king is among them.
NASB.22: 'God brings them out of Egypt, He is for them like the horns of the wild ox.
NASB.23: 'For there is no omen against Jacob, Nor is there any divination against Israel; At the proper time it shall be said to Jacob And to Israel, what God has done!
NASB.24: 'Behold, a people rises like a lioness, And as a lion it lifts itself; It will not lie down until it devours the prey, And drinks the blood of the slain.'
NASB.25: Then Balak said to Balaam, 'Do not curse them at all nor bless them at all!'
NASB.26: But Balaam replied to Balak, 'Did I not tell you, 'Whatever the LORD speaks, that I must do '?'
NASB.27: Then Balak said to Balaam, 'Please come, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will be agreeable with God that you curse them for me from there.'
NASB.28: So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor which overlooks the wasteland.
NASB.29: Balaam said to Balak, 'Build seven altars for me here and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.'
NASB.30: Balak did just as Balaam had said, and offered up a bull and a ram on [each] altar.

NLT.1: Then Balaam said to King Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven young bulls and seven rams for me to sacrifice.”
NLT.2: Balak followed his instructions, and the two of them sacrificed a young bull and a ram on each altar.
NLT.3: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here by your burnt offerings, and I will go to see if the LORD will respond to me. Then I will tell you whatever he reveals to me.” So Balaam went alone to the top of a bare hill,
NLT.4: and God met him there. Balaam said to him, “I have prepared seven altars and have sacrificed a young bull and a ram on each altar.”
NLT.5: The LORD gave Balaam a message for King Balak. Then he said, “Go back to Balak and give him my message.”
NLT.6: So Balaam returned and found the king standing beside his burnt offerings with all the officials of Moab.
NLT.7:
This was the message Balaam delivered: “Balak summoned me to come from Aram;
the king of Moab brought me from the eastern hills.
‘Come,’ he said, ‘curse Jacob for me!
Come and announce Israel’s doom.’
NLT.8:
But how can I curse those
whom God has not cursed?
How can I condemn those
whom the LORD has not condemned?
NLT.9:
I see them from the cliff tops;
I watch them from the hills.
I see a people who live by themselves,
set apart from other nations.
NLT.10:
Who can count Jacob’s descendants, as numerous as dust?
Who can count even a fourth of Israel’s people?
Let me die like the righteous;
let my life end like theirs.”
NLT.11: Then King Balak demanded of Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies. Instead, you have blessed them!”
NLT.12: But Balaam replied, “I will speak only the message that the LORD puts in my mouth.”
NLT.13: Then King Balak told him, “Come with me to another place. There you will see another part of the nation of Israel, but not all of them. Curse at least that many!”
NLT.14: So Balak took Balaam to the plateau of Zophim on Pisgah Peak. He built seven altars there and offered a young bull and a ram on each altar.
NLT.15: Then Balaam said to the king, “Stand here by your burnt offerings while I go over there to meet the LORD.”
NLT.16: And the LORD met Balaam and gave him a message. Then he said, “Go back to Balak and give him my message.”
NLT.17: So Balaam returned and found the king standing beside his burnt offerings with all the officials of Moab. “What did the LORD say?” Balak asked eagerly.
NLT.18:
This was the message Balaam delivered: “Rise up, Balak, and listen!
Hear me, son of Zippor.
NLT.19:
God is not a man, so he does not lie.
He is not human, so he does not change his mind.
Has he ever spoken and failed to act?
Has he ever promised and not carried it through?
NLT.20:
Listen, I received a command to bless;
God has blessed, and I cannot reverse it!
NLT.21:
No misfortune is in his plan for Jacob;
no trouble is in store for Israel.
For the LORD their God is with them;
he has been proclaimed their king.
NLT.22:
God brought them out of Egypt;
for them he is as strong as a wild ox.
NLT.23:
No curse can touch Jacob;
no magic has any power against Israel.
For now it will be said of Jacob,
‘What wonders God has done for Israel!’
NLT.24:
These people rise up like a lioness,
like a majestic lion rousing itself.
They refuse to rest
until they have feasted on prey,
drinking the blood of the slaughtered!”
NLT.25: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Fine, but if you won’t curse them, at least don’t bless them!”
NLT.26: But Balaam replied to Balak, “Didn’t I tell you that I can do only what the LORD tells me?”
NLT.27: Then King Balak said to Balaam, “Come, I will take you to one more place. Perhaps it will please God to let you curse them from there.”
NLT.28: So Balak took Balaam to the top of Mount Peor, overlooking the wasteland.
NLT.29: Balaam again told Balak, “Build me seven altars, and prepare seven young bulls and seven rams for me to sacrifice.”
NLT.30: So Balak did as Balaam ordered and offered a young bull and a ram on each altar.

WEB.1: Balaam said to Balak, “Build here seven altars for me, and prepare here seven bulls and seven rams for me.”
WEB.2: Balak did as Balaam had spoken; and Balak and Balaam offered on every altar a bull and a ram.
WEB.3: Balaam said to Balak, “Stand by your burnt offering, and I will go. Perhaps Yahweh will come to meet me. Whatever he shows me I will tell you.” He went to a bare height.
WEB.4: God met Balaam, and he said to him, “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.”
WEB.5: Yahweh put a word in Balaam’s mouth, and said, “Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.”
WEB.6: He returned to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, he, and all the princes of Moab.
WEB.7: He took up his parable, and said, “From Aram has Balak brought me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the East. Come, curse Jacob for me. Come, defy Israel.
WEB.8: How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? How shall I defy whom Yahweh has not defied?
WEB.9: For from the top of the rocks I see him. From the hills I see him. Behold, it is a people that dwells alone, and shall not be listed among the nations.
WEB.10: Who can count the dust of Jacob, or count the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous! Let my last end be like his!”
WEB.11: Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them altogether.”
WEB.12: He answered and said, “Must I not take heed to speak that which Yahweh puts in my mouth?”
WEB.13: Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, where you may see them. You shall see just part of them, and shall not see them all. Curse them from there for me.”
WEB.14: He took him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.
WEB.15: He said to Balak, “Stand here by your burnt offering, while I meet over there.”
WEB.16: Yahweh met Balaam, and put a word in his mouth, and said, “Return to Balak, and say this.”
WEB.17: He came to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him. Balak said to him, “What has Yahweh spoken?”
WEB.18: He took up his parable, and said, “Rise up, Balak, and hear! Listen to me, you son of Zippor.
WEB.19: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor the son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not make it good?
WEB.20: Behold, I have received a command to bless. He has blessed, and I can’t reverse it.
WEB.21: He has not seen iniquity in Jacob. Neither has he seen perverseness in Israel. Yahweh his God is with him. The shout of a king is among them.
WEB.22: God brings them out of Egypt. He has as it were the strength of the wild ox.
WEB.23: Surely there is no enchantment with Jacob; Neither is there any divination with Israel. Now it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, ‘What has God done!’
WEB.24: Behold, the people rises up as a lioness. As a lion he lifts himself up. He shall not lie down until he eats of the prey, and drinks the blood of the slain.”
WEB.25: Balak said to Balaam, “Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all.”

WEB.27: Balak said to Balaam, “Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.”
WEB.28: Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, that looks down on the desert.
WEB.29: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
WEB.30: Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.

AMP.1: Then Balaam said to Balak, "Build seven altars for me here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams here."
AMP.2: Balak did just as Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
AMP.3: Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stand beside your burnt offering and I will go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me; and whatever He shows me I will tell you." So he went to a desolate hill.
AMP.4: Now God met Balaam, who said to Him, "I have prepared seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each altar."
AMP.5: Then the LORD put a speech in Balaam's mouth, and said, "Return to Balak, and you shall speak thus."
AMP.6: Balaam returned to Balak, and behold, he was standing by his burnt sacrifice, he and all the leaders of Moab.
AMP.7:
Balaam took up his [first] discourse (oracle) and said:
"Balak, the king of Moab, has brought me from Aram (Syria),
from the mountains of the east, [saying,]
'Come, curse [the descendants of] Jacob for me;
And come, [violently] denounce Israel.'
AMP.8:
"How shall I curse those whom God has not cursed?
Or how can I [violently] denounce those the LORD has not denounced?
AMP.9:
"For from the top of the rocks I see Israel,
And from the hills I look at him.
Behold, the people [of Israel] shall dwell alone
And will not be reckoned among the nations.
AMP.10:
"Who can count the dust (the descendants) of Jacob
And the number of even the fourth part of Israel?
Let me die the death of the righteous [those who are upright and in right standing with God],
And let my end be like his!"
AMP.11: Then Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, but here you have [thoroughly] blessed them instead!"
AMP.12: Balaam answered, "Must I not be obedient and careful to speak what the LORD has put in my mouth?"
AMP.13: Balak said to him, "Come with me, I implore you, to another place from where you can see them, although you will see only the nearest and not all of them; and curse them for me from there."
AMP.14: So he took Balaam to the field of Zophim to the top of [Mount] Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
AMP.15: Balaam said to Balak, "Stand here beside your burnt offering while I go to meet the LORD over there."
AMP.16: Then the LORD met Balaam and put a speech in his mouth, and said, "Go back to Balak and you shall speak thus."
AMP.17: When Balaam returned to Balak, he was standing beside his burnt offering, and the leaders of Moab were with him. And Balak said to him, "What has the LORD spoken?"
AMP.18:
Balaam took up his [second] discourse (oracle) and said:
"Rise up, O Balak, and hear;
Listen [closely] to me, son of Zippor.
AMP.19:
"God is not a man, that He should lie,
Nor a son of man, that He should repent.
Has He said, and will He not do it?
Or has He spoken and will He not make it good and fulfill it?
AMP.20:
"Behold, I have received His command to bless [Israel].
He has blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
AMP.21:
"God has not observed wickedness in Jacob [for he is forgiven],
Nor has He seen trouble in Israel.
The LORD their God is with Israel,
And the shout of their King is among the people.
AMP.22:
"God brought them out of Egypt;
They have the strength of a wild ox.
AMP.23:
"For there is no enchantment or omen against Jacob,
Nor is there any divination against Israel.
At the proper time it shall be said to Jacob
And to Israel, what has God done!
AMP.24:
"Behold, a people rises up like a lioness
And lifts itself up like a lion;
He will not lie down until he devours the prey
And drinks the blood of the slain."
AMP.25: Then Balak said to Balaam, "Neither curse them at all nor bless them at all!"
AMP.26: But Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not say to you, 'All that the LORD speaks, that I must do?'"
AMP.27: Then Balak said to Balaam, "Please come; I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God to let you curse them for me from there."
AMP.28: So Balak brought Balaam to the top of [Mount] Peor, that overlooks the wasteland.
AMP.29: And Balaam said to Balak, "Build seven altars for me here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams here."
AMP.30: Balak did just as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

NRSVCE.19:
God is not a human being, that he should lie,
or a mortal, that he should change his mind.
Has he promised, and will he not do it?
Has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
NRSVCE.20:
See, I received a command to bless;
he has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.
NRSVCE.21:
He has not beheld misfortune in Jacob;
nor has he seen trouble in Israel.
The LORD their God is with them,
acclaimed as a king among them.
NRSVCE.22:
God, who brings them out of Egypt,
is like the horns of a wild ox for them.
NRSVCE.23:
Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob,
no divination against Israel;
now it shall be said of Jacob and Israel,
‘See what God has done!’
NRSVCE.24:
Look, a people rising up like a lioness,
and rousing itself like a lion!
It does not lie down until it has eaten the prey
and drunk the blood of the slain.”
NRSVCE.25: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all.”
NRSVCE.26: But Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell you, ‘Whatever the LORD says, that is what I must do’?”
NRSVCE.27: So Balak said to Balaam, “Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.”
NRSVCE.28: So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
NRSVCE.29: Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me.”
NRSVCE.30: So Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
